insight:
The file__apply_diff tool's OLD matching behavior (contiguous contextBefore+oldLines+contextAfter block, interleaved context dropped) repeatedly failed to apply patches during the very rewrite that fixed those problems. This is strong evidence the redesign was needed. When rewriting a patch/diff tool, expect the tool to fail against its own source files until the rewrite lands — plan to use file__write (full rewrites) or external scripts (python) for surgical edits instead of the patch tool itself.

Aggressive format-aware fuzz (collapse all whitespace including newlines) does NOT normalize punctuation. Test data for line-break reflow cases must account for trailing commas: `foo(a,b,c,)` (prettier-style trailing comma) collapses to a different string than `foo(a,b,c)` (no trailing comma). This is by design (whitespace-only normalization), but LLM-generated patches that differ in punctuation will not match even at the aggressive level. If this becomes a real-world problem, a future extension could add punctuation normalization to the aggressive level.

When splitting a file into a directory of the same name (e.g., patch-applier.ts → patch-applier/), TypeScript resolves `./patch-applier/types.js` to `patch-applier/types.ts` even when `patch-applier.ts` exists. The `.ts`/`.js` extension in the import specifier disambiguates. This works cleanly but is a naming collision worth documenting for maintainers.

AppliedHunk needed a hunkIndex field (not in the original plan) so the tool wrapper can correlate applied hunks back to their original positions for diff rendering. Without it, the diffHunks construction in file.ts was a mess of placeholder hacks. When designing a partial-success API, always include the original index on each success record so callers can correlate.

file__apply_diff fuzz-matching can silently corrupt files when hunks are too small/under-anchored: in one session it dropped a freshly-added type declaration and duplicated the file's trailing ~5 lines (both via 'fuzz: 0' matches) when two similar hunks were applied in sequence. Symptom: tsc errors at EOF or 'no exported member'. Mitigation: (1) always re-read the file (esp. the tail + the edited region) immediately after each apply_diff, (2) anchor hunks with more surrounding context (the @@ section heading + several context lines), and (3) apply edits that touch the same file's nearby regions serially, not in parallel. When corruption is detected, repair surgically rather than re-applying blindly.
